title: Format a typed score
summary: Java variables have static types; local var infers a type from an initializer.
rules: Use equals for string content; == compares reference identity.
var is for initialized local variables, not fields or method parameters.
Primitive int is not nullable; Integer is its boxed reference type.

references.title: Format a typed score — official guide

title: Total only even values
summary: Branches select work; loops repeat work and can skip or stop iterations.
rules: Conditions must be boolean.
Enhanced for iterates arrays and Iterable values.
Switch expressions must be exhaustive and can use yield in block arms.

references.title: Total only even values — official guide

title: Clamp a value with a reusable method
summary: Methods declare parameter and return types; static methods belong to the class.
syntax:
ReturnType method(Type parameter) { return expression; }
static ReturnType utility(Type parameter) { return expression; }
rules: Java passes all arguments by value, including object references.
Overloads differ in parameter types, not return type alone.
Validate preconditions before doing work.

references.title: Clamp a value with a reusable method — official guide

title: Encapsulate a visit counter
summary: Classes combine state, constructors and methods with access control.
rules: Constructors have the class name and no return type.
private fields hide mutable implementation details.
A public top-level class uses a file with the same name.

references.title: Encapsulate a visit counter — official guide

title: Inject a greeting strategy
summary: Interfaces describe behavior; a single abstract method can be implemented by a lambda.
rules: Implementing methods cannot reduce interface method visibility.
A functional interface has one abstract method.
Prefer accepting a behavior contract when callers should choose the implementation.

references.title: Inject a greeting strategy — official guide

title: Validate an immutable order value
summary: Records provide component accessors, value equality and a canonical constructor.
rules: Records are final and cannot extend another class.
Components are final references; referenced mutable objects are not made immutable.
Records were finalized in Java 16. Compact constructors validate before component assignment.

references.title: Validate an immutable order value — official guide

title: Copy values from a covariant source
summary: Type parameters make reusable APIs type safe; wildcards describe producer and consumer variance.
rules: List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>.
A producer uses extends; a consumer uses super.
Generic type arguments are reference types, so use Integer rather than int.

references.title: Copy values from a covariant source — official guide

title: Count words in insertion order
summary: Lists preserve sequence, sets enforce uniqueness, and maps associate keys with values.
rules: List.of, Set.of and Map.of are unmodifiable and reject null elements.
HashMap has no stable iteration order; LinkedHashMap retains insertion order.
Use equals/hashCode consistently for map keys and set elements.

references.title: Count words in insertion order — official guide

title: Filter and sort positive values
summary: Streams describe lazy transformations followed by a terminal operation.
syntax: source.stream().filter(predicate).map(transform).sorted().toList();
rules: A stream is consumed once; build another for a second traversal.
toList returns an unmodifiable list (Java 16+).
Keep pipeline functions free of shared mutable side effects.

references.title: Filter and sort positive values — official guide

title: Group order quantities by name
summary: Collectors combine stream elements into maps, groups or scalar aggregates.
syntax:
stream.collect(Collectors.groupingBy(keyFunction, downstreamCollector));
Collectors.summingInt(valueFunction);
rules: groupingBy rejects null classifier keys.
Supply a map factory when deterministic key order matters.
Downstream collectors aggregate values inside each group.

references.title: Group order quantities by name — official guide

title: Normalize an optional display name
summary: Optional represents a result that may be absent, with explicit transformations and fallbacks.
syntax: Optional.ofNullable(value).filter(predicate).map(transform).orElseGet(supplier);
rules: Use ofNullable for nullable inputs; of rejects null.
orElse eagerly evaluates its argument; orElseGet evaluates only when empty.
Avoid unchecked get; prefer a fallback or orElseThrow.

references.title: Normalize an optional display name — official guide

title: Report a malformed quantity with its cause
summary: Exceptions separate successful values from failure; checked exceptions must be caught or declared.
rules: Catch the narrowest failure you can handle; preserve the cause when translating.
RuntimeException is unchecked; IOException is checked.
Do not silently swallow failures or use exceptions for ordinary absence.

references.title: Report a malformed quantity with its cause — official guide

title: Close a line reader on success and failure
summary: Try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable resources when control leaves the block.
syntax: try (Resource resource = open()) { use(resource); }
rules: Multiple resources close in reverse declaration order.
If both body and close fail, the close failure is suppressed on the original exception.
Files.lines creates a stream that also needs closing.

references.title: Close a line reader on success and failure — official guide

title: Write and read a UTF-8 report
summary: Path identifies a location; Files offers checked I/O operations with explicit encodings.
rules: Default writeString options create or truncate the destination.
Use a disposable directory for experiments and propagate or handle IOException.
resolve builds paths; never assume untrusted paths stay inside a parent directory.

references.title: Write and read a UTF-8 report — official guide

title: Compose an asynchronous calculation
summary: CompletableFuture represents a pending value with success and failure continuations.
rules: join throws CompletionException for failed computations.
Supply an executor for controlled lifecycle and blocking tasks.
Cancellation is cooperative and does not guarantee interrupting underlying work.

references.title: Compose an asynchronous calculation — official guide

title: Collect worker results and close the executor
summary: Executors schedule work; Future retrieves its result or reports failure.
rules: ExecutorService is AutoCloseable starting in Java 19; this example targets 21.
get can throw InterruptedException, ExecutionException or TimeoutException.
Avoid unsynchronized shared state; combine returned values on the caller thread.

references.title: Collect worker results and close the executor — official guide

title: Sort names using a static import
summary: Packages group types; imports let source refer to types and static members by short names.
rules: Place package declarations before imports.
Wildcard imports do not include subpackages.
Standard Maven paths mirror package names under src/main/java and src/test/java; see the separate tooling guide.

references.title: Sort names using a static import — official guide

title: Assert values and failures with JUnit Jupiter
summary: JUnit Jupiter discovers @Test methods and reports assertion failures with useful diagnostics.
rules: Use org.junit.jupiter.api.Test, not JUnit 4 annotations.
Tests need the Jupiter engine at runtime; spring-boot-starter-test includes it.
Keep tests independent; exception assertions should exercise the precise failing operation.

references.title: Assert values and failures with JUnit Jupiter — official guide

title: Test clamp boundaries with parameterized cases
summary: Parameterized tests run a test method once per supplied argument row.
rules: junit-jupiter-params supplies parameterized annotations and argument sources.
CsvSource converts text cells to parameter types; quoted empty text differs from null.
Use MethodSource for complex objects or computed argument streams.

references.title: Test clamp boundaries with parameterized cases — official guide

title: Round-trip an order through Jackson JSON
summary: Jackson databind maps JSON to Java values and back with an ObjectMapper.
rules: Reuse a configured ObjectMapper; configure it before concurrent use.
This catalog uses Jackson 2.x com.fasterxml.jackson imports, not Jackson 3.
Record support is built in; date/time types need the appropriate module.

references.title: Round-trip an order through Jackson JSON — official guide

title: Handle malformed or unexpected JSON
summary: Jackson distinguishes syntax/mapping failures; deserialization policy controls unknown fields.
rules: Jackson core parsing and databind mapping failures derive from JsonProcessingException.
Unknown-field policy can differ between a standalone mapper and a framework-configured mapper.
Successful mapping is not business validation; validate required fields separately.

references.title: Handle malformed or unexpected JSON — official guide

title: Serve and create a validated JSON order
summary: Spring MVC maps HTTP requests to controller methods and converts values through message converters.
rules: spring-boot-starter-web provides MVC/Jackson; add starter-validation for Jakarta validation.
Place controllers under the application component-scan package.
Use explicit status codes and validate external input before doing business work.

references.title: Serve and create a validated JSON order — official guide

title: Validate order values before a service call
summary: Jakarta Bean Validation declares field constraints; Spring applies @Valid to request bodies.
syntax:
record Input(@NotBlank String name, @Positive int quantity) {}
Set<ConstraintViolation<Input>> errors = validator.validate(input);
rules: Use jakarta.validation with Spring Boot 3; javax.validation is from the older namespace.
Constraints run only when a validator is invoked or framework validation is enabled.
@Positive accepts null on boxed values; combine @NotNull when a boxed value is required.

references.title: Validate order values before a service call — official guide

title: Return stable JSON errors for invalid requests
summary: Controller advice translates known exceptions into a consistent HTTP error contract.
rules: Catch known exceptions narrowly; do not disguise unexpected server errors as client errors.
Invalid request bodies and failed field constraints are different exception types.
Return stable public messages and keep internal exception details out of the response.

references.title: Return stable JSON errors for invalid requests — official guide

title: Test JSON requests without a listening server
summary: MockMvc exercises Spring MVC routing, JSON conversion and validation in process.
rules: SpringBootTest loads the application; WebMvcTest is a focused MVC slice with different bean requirements.
Test response bodies and failures as well as status codes.
MockMvc needs no real port or external service and is not a browser test.

references.title: Test JSON requests without a listening server — official guide
